newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ease ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ease ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended slightly easier in very thin trade on Tuesday as players adjusted their positions ahead of a heavy calendar of U.S. economic data.
"We have quite a few numbers out of the U.S. this week and if there is any kind of major reaction in U.S. treasuries, it'll probably be to the downside," a trader with a U.S. house said.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.375 against their IMM close at 93.395 on light volume of 6,785 lots. Near-term support is seen at 93.350.
"The market is still prone to some downside. Once we get out of the Golden Week holiday period, December Euroyen could even go below 98.90," the trader said.
Japanese government bond futures for June were not traded due to the holiday.
The quarterly U.S. employment cost index (ECI), due at 1230 GMT, and the non-farm payrolls report for April on Friday are among the highlights on this week's schedule of indicators.
According to a Reuters poll of economists, the ECI was expected to be up 0.9 percent in the first quarter after rising 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.

Euroyen futures saw slow trade with Tokyo markets closed for a holiday. After hovering in a one-tick band, December Euroyen stood at 98.98 around 1130 GMT, unchanged against their IMM close. Volume was a low 1,080 lots.
